title: OOP & Software Design
goal: Learn where logic belongs and make responsibilities explicit.

topics.title: Responsibility
topics.description: Give each object a clear reason to exist and a bounded set of duties.
learningGoals: Give each object a clear reason to exist and a bounded set of duties.
Explain the tradeoffs and demonstrate one failure or boundary case.
examples: Apply responsibility to a session, coupon, or token lifecycle. Compare a successful operation with one that must be rejected.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

topics.title: Information expert
topics.description: Place behavior with the object that owns the information it needs.
learningGoals: Place behavior with the object that owns the information it needs.
Explain Data ownership, Behavior placement and Invariants.
Demonstrate a valid operation and a boundary or failure case.
examples: BankAccount owns its balance and frozen state, so it decides whether withdrawal is allowed.

tasks.title: Explain Information expert in your own words
Work through the example and predict the result
Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help

topics.title: Tell, don't ask
topics.description: Ask objects to perform behavior instead of inspecting and mutating their state.
learningGoals: Ask objects to perform behavior instead of inspecting and mutating their state.
Explain Behavior-oriented APIs, Encapsulation and Decision ownership.
Demonstrate a valid operation and a boundary or failure case.
examples: Call account.withdraw(amount) instead of reading balance, checking it in a service, then calling setBalance.

tasks.title: Explain Tell, don't ask in your own words

Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help
